findings.issue: The website does not list the LSPs (EduPay and MediQuick) or their DLAs, nor does it provide details of the activities for which they have been engaged.
findings.doc_evidence: Website: Saraswati Finance's website has a page listing its own app. It does not list EduPay, MediQuick or their apps, or what each is engaged for, and it has no link to RBI's CMS or Sachet portal.
findings.fix: Update the website to include a dedicated section listing all LSPs (such as EduPay and MediQuick) along with their DLAs and the specific activities for which they have been engaged.
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph [DLD2025:8(iv)] requires that the RE's website must include details of LSPs and the DLAs of the LSPs along with the details of the activities for which they have been engaged. The product feature explicitly states that the website does not list EduPay, MediQuick, or their apps, nor does it provide details of the activities for which they have been engaged. Therefore, the feature fails to comply with the requirement specified in the paragraph.

findings.issue: The contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officer are not prominently displayed on the websites of the RE, its LSP, or on the DLA. They are only provided in the KFS.
findings.doc_evidence: 2. Grievance officer: Saraswati Finance has a named nodal grievance officer. Their contact details are given only in the KFS; they are not shown on the website or in either partner app.
findings.fix: Display the contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officer in a prominent and easily accessible location on the RE's website, LSP websites, and DLAs.
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph requires that the contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officer be prominently displayed on the websites of the RE, its LSP, and on the DLA, as well as in the KFS. The product feature states that the contact details are only provided in the KFS and not on the website or in either partner app. This means that the contact details are not displayed on the websites of the RE or its LSP, nor on the DLA, which is a violation of the RBI requirement.

findings.issue: The facility of lodging a complaint is not made available on the DLA or on the website, as required by the RBI.
findings.doc_evidence: 3. Complaints: Borrowers cannot lodge a complaint in the partner apps or on the website; they must visit a branch.
findings.fix: Implement a complaint lodging facility on the DLA and the RE's website, ensuring it is user-friendly and accessible to all borrowers and users.
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph requires that the facility of lodging a complaint be made available on the DLA and on the website. The product feature states that borrowers cannot lodge a complaint on the website or in the partner apps, and that the contact details of the grievance officer are only available in the KFS, not on the website. This means that the facility of lodging a complaint is not available on the website, which violates the requirement stated in the RBI paragraph.

summary: The compliance review of Saraswati Finance's Digital Lending Disclosures identified three medium-severity gaps. First, the website does not list the LSPs (EduPay and MediQuick) or their DLAs, nor does it provide details of the activities for which they have been engaged, as required under DLD2025:8(iv). Second, the contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officer are not prominently displayed on the websites of the RE, its LSP, or on the DLA, as mandated by DLD2025:11(ii). Third, the facility of lodging a complaint is not made available on the DLA or on the website, as required by DLD2025:11(iii).
